SELECTED_INDEX: 2
CONFIDENCE: 0.46
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows (1) a very strong C=O stretch at 1737 cm⁻¹, typical for a non-conjugated ester carbonyl; (2) a medium band at 1651 cm⁻¹ that fits an isolated C=C stretch; (3) the pair 995 / 953 cm⁻¹ and an additional band at 839–872 cm⁻¹, characteristic of the =CH₂ out-of-plane wags and twists of a terminal vinyl group; (4) a strong C–O/CO stretch near 1294 cm⁻¹ expected for esters; and (5) C–H stretches for both sp² (3022, 3098 cm⁻¹) and sp³ (2888–2997 cm⁻¹) sites.  

Among the candidates, only molecule 2 (C=CCOC=O, vinyl formate) simultaneously contains (a) a saturated ester C=O, (b) a terminal vinyl group, and (c) no O–H or N–H groups (absence of 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ band). Other ester-containing candidates either have an O–H stretch that is not observed (5), or carbonyl types expected at lower frequency (1: conjugated ketone; 3: thio-ester; 7: mixed anhydride/aldehyde). Therefore candidate 2 best explains the key Raman features.
